newsitem.title: CANADA: Report concludes Busang claim based on false data.
newsitem.headline: Report concludes Busang claim based on false data.

text.p: Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals said on Sunday that an independent report concluded that the company's claims for the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia were based on falsified data.

"We share the shock and dismay of our shareholders and others that the gold we thought we had at Busang now appears not to be there," Bre-X chairman and chief executive officer David Walsh said in a statement on Sunday.
In an interim report to Bre-X, consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. said an "economic gold deposit has not been identified in the southeast zone of the Busang property, and is unlikely to be."
Bre-X hired Strathcona in March after doubts emerged about the size of the Busang deposit, estimated by Bre-X at 71 million ounces and touted as the century's biggest gold find.
But Strathcona said it found evidence of tampering with Bre-X's core samples taken from the Busang project, located deep in the jungles of Borneo.

"The magnitude of the tampering with core samples that we believe has occurred and resulting falsification of assay values at Busang, is of a scale and over a period of time and with a precision that, to our knowledge, is without precedent in the history of mining anywhere in the world," the report said.
